quote: And do you have a battery?
stewart_read: Customer volunteers interest in battery backup unprompted — a strong buying signal Ion can act on (Tesla Powerwall).
coaching_implication: Rep confirms availability but doesn't flag this to the closer or use it to build curiosity ('great question — we'll dig into battery sizing at your appointment'); should be surfaced explicitly in the handoff.

quote: So my only, worry is that there so our panels are 440 watt panels.
stewart_read: Rep gets pulled into a technical debate about panel wattage and count instead of redirecting to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have been trying to reassure the customer his numbers weren't wrong, but the depth of explanation goes beyond what's needed to book.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch line — 'that's exactly what our specialist will size for you at the appointment' — instead of engaging on panel specs.

stewart_read: Customer doesn't understand the incentive framing; rep recovers by explaining state/veteran incentives reasonably clearly.
coaching_implication: Handled adequately — rep clarified rather than dodging, but could tie back to bill savings instead of generic incentive talk.

quote: But this guy told me that from Sunrise, there was gonna spent a great big beautiful bill next to them.
stewart_read: Customer references a Sunrun rep's specific claim about legislation but rep never asks what exactly was quoted or promised.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the comment as a passing remark not worth chasing rather than a competitive intel opportunity.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what did Sunrun quote you?' to surface competitive context per verify.prior_designs coaching notes.

quote: So on your comment bill, would you mind just sending me a photo of that usage just so I can make sure that I get it as accurate as possible?
stewart_read: Rep has the $151.50 bill number in hand but never reflects it back as pain leverage before pivoting straight into logistics of photo capture.
coaching_implication: Should flip the $151.50 into 'that's real money going to the utility every month — let's see what solar could redirect' before asking for the photo.

quote: It's not gonna take too much longer, is it?
stewart_read: Customer signals fatigue with the process; rep reassures briefly but doesn't acknowledge the frustration directly.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's 'this is just the last thing that I need' is a minimal but functional reassurance, so this may be a low-severity miss.
coaching_implication: A quick acknowledgment ('sorry this is taking a minute') would land better than a flat procedural answer.

quote: My mom passed away. We're having a funeral on May 2, so it's gonna have to be after that.
stewart_read: Rep offers a brief condolence but immediately moves to reschedule logistics without pausing on the disclosure.
alternative_hypothesis: Time constraints of a setter call may justify a quick pivot rather than dwelling, since the customer himself moved on quickly.
coaching_implication: A slightly longer acknowledgment before jumping to 'the fourth or the fifth' would honor the trust gift better.
